q: In this position paper, we argue that to claim a “long-horizon failure”, benchmarks must compare actual full-task success against a baseline prediction built from short, individual stages.
r: EC3: position paper proposing a benchmark-design argument with no experiment, not SDD or a development-task evaluation.

q: we present the first systematic study of native dynamic concurrency in three frontier coding agents: Codex, Claude Code, and Kimi Code. We conduct controlled comparisons with dynamic concurrency enabled or disabled
r: Include: controlled matched comparison of coding agents on long-horizon repository-construction tasks with token cost and success metrics.

q: we present OCTAVE, a benchmark for complete HTML5 game generation that organizes tasks around capability coverage
r: EC6: benchmark limited to one specialised domain (HTML5 games), main contribution is the benchmark, not a general evaluation method.

q: we add a prompt-only variant of model-managed context: two tools and one paragraph of guidance, without training or scaffolding, in a local agent, CTXAGENT.
r: EC5: new context-management agent evaluated on a benchmark assembled from existing ones, not SDD or context files.

q: agents maintain packages in the world with a high-level goal of improving software efficiency
r: EC6: task is optimising speed of existing packages in a simulation, not building software from requirements.

q: A systematic literature review of 628 primary studies (July 2021 to October 2026)
r: IC1: review of techniques for the quality of LLM-generated code, mostly non-agentic; not SDD, context files or coding-agent evaluation.

q: We introduce MITL (Metrics-In-TheLoop), a lightweight plugin that measures the code an agent has just changed, provides feedback to the agent in the form of a short report before the agent continues
r: EC5: new inference-time feedback technique tested on existing benchmarks (Commit0, SlopCodeBench, SWE-EVO).

q: benchmark of 46 long-horizon tasks spanning nine categories, including experiment reproduction, software engineering, multimodal analysis, interactive games,
r: EC6: general terminal tasks, mostly not code development of an application.
